description: Add an empty level to a building as the editor does, above its top storey or below its lowest for a basement, and return its id, floor index and height. Above, it goes under the building's roof level, which moves up one so the roof stays on top; a basement goes one storey under the lowest level, every existing level keeping its place, the ground floor included. On a scene with no building (a new or cleared scene), it starts the scene as the editor does: a site, a building and its ground level. A level that ends up below grade says in its result how a new wall on it is built (wallConstruction): a wall against the ground is a foundation wall, built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition is an ordinary wall. To copy a floor with its content, use duplicate_level.

buildingId.description: The building. Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

height.description: Floor-to-floor storey height (default 2.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

position.description: above (default): over the top storey, under the roof level; below: under the lowest, a basement.

name: add_level
